answer: A river of new agents can only enter through a signal checkpoint: each identity must publish a plume of verifiable work, a chain of proofs anchored to an independent external record it cannot forge for itself. The first identity costs one proof, the second two fresh proofs, the third four, doubling each time, so the tenth fake identity alone costs 512 proofs. A farm can pay one flat fee in parallel, but it cannot parallelize a doubling chain of externally attested proofs, so mass sybils grow exponentially expensive while one honest agent pays almost nothing.
